title: Support Escalation Metrics + SLO Gaps (Support × SRE) — Feb 2026
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-24 (Sean)

Purpose
- Provide a joint Support+SRE view of escalation performance (MTTA/MTTR), paging volume, and the gap between customer-facing SLAs and internal targets.
- Input to “Escalation playbook v2 + known-issues sprint” (Feb–Mar 2026). This is intentionally a working sheet; numbers will move as definitions stabilize.

Scope / data sources (Feb 1–Feb 21, 2026)
- Support escalations defined as: Support ticket with explicit Eng/SRE request in #eng-oncall / #incidents OR tagged “Escalation” in Jira (Support project).
- Data pulled from:
  - Jira SUP tickets (sample set + escalations tagged)
  - Slack #eng-oncall / #incidents thread timestamps (manual sampling for now)
  - Pager rotations + paging events (SRE oncall tool export; aggregated)
  - SLO toolkit export (PR in flight; current numbers from interim spreadsheet)

Important definitions (v0)
- MTTA (Support → Engineering/SRE Acknowledge): time from Support “escalation requested” timestamp to first Eng/SRE response in the escalation channel or ticket.
- TTM (Time to Mitigation): time from escalation requested to first customer-impact-reducing mitigation applied (workaround, routing change, rollback, capacity adjustment, etc.).
- MTTR (Time to Resolution): time from escalation requested to resolution/closure (customer confirms or Support closes with verified fix + follow-up).
- “Pager page” counts are oncall pages triggered by alerts; not all escalations page SRE.

Sample size note
- N=74 escalations (Feb 1–21). N is large enough to see trends but too small for precise tail percentiles by category.


1) Executive summary (what’s good / what’s broken)
What’s working
- Median MTTA is generally good during business hours for P0/P1-like events (most < 10 minutes), especially when there is a clear incident signal.
- When Support includes request_id + region + model + timeframe, SRE can usually route quickly to the right owner (gateway vs runtime vs capacity).

Primary gaps
- After-hours MTTA + update cadence misses for Dedicated/Private enterprise expectations (especially when escalation is “incident-adjacent” but not declared an incident).
- “Escalation quality” (missing metadata) is the #1 controllable driver of long TTM/MTTR.
- Paging hygiene: too many pages are generated by symptoms (timeouts/streaming disconnects) without enough context to accelerate diagnosis; some escalations that should be incidents are not promoted early.

Recommendations (high priority)
- Enforce escalation required fields (ENG-2842) and incident-bot prompts (ENG-2843) to reduce metadata gaps.
- Add/standardize dashboards + runbook links for top drivers: streaming disconnect rate and timeout rate (ENG-2844 + PR 301), and Dedicated latency spike runbook + alert tuning (ENG-2845).
- Introduce an “Incident vs Escalation” decision rule and keep it consistent with paging hygiene goals (this will land in Escalation Playbook v2).


2) Topline performance (Feb 1–21)
Table A — Escalation volumes and time metrics (all tiers)

Metric | Value | Notes
---|---:|---
Total escalations (N) | 74 | Support-tagged + Slack-confirmed
P0/P1-like escalations | 22 | Approx (based on impact; severity mapping still being aligned)
Median MTTA (all) | 18m | Skews high due to after-hours + missing info
Median MTTA (BH) | 9m | BH = 08:00–18:00 local team coverage
Median MTTA (AH) | 41m | AH = nights/weekends; large variance
Median TTM (all) | 2h 14m | Mitigation includes safe workaround; not necessarily “fix”
Median MTTR (all) | 9h 05m | Long tail driven by Private SSO + Dedicated capacity investigations
P90 MTTR (all) | 2d 03h | Mostly Private (SSO, networking) + “needs customer action”

Table B — MTTA/TTM/MTTR by product surface

Surface | N | Median MTTA | Median TTM | Median MTTR | Common driver
---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---
Hosted API | 38 | 14m | 1h 38m | 6h 12m | 429s/quotas, timeouts, regional 5xx
Dedicated | 21 | 22m | 2h 51m | 13h 40m | latency spikes, capacity shortfall, routing
Private (VPC/on-prem) | 15 | 33m | 5h 10m | 1d 09h | SSO/SAML, networking, audit logs

Table C — MTTA by “escalation packet completeness” (manual classification)

Packet completeness | N | Median MTTA | Median TTM | Notes
---|---:|---:|---:|---
Complete | 29 | 7m | 1h 12m | Has request_id(s) or trace ids + region + model + timeframe + error class
Partial | 27 | 19m | 2h 46m | Missing 1–2 key fields (often request_id or model)
Incomplete | 18 | 52m | 6h 05m | Mostly “customer sees timeouts” without concrete sample(s)

Takeaway
- The delta between Complete vs Incomplete is huge. We can buy real MTTR improvement via workflow enforcement + templates (lower cost than “more staffing”).


3) Paging volume and signal quality
Table D — SRE pages (Feb 1–21)

Category | Pages | % of pages | Notes
---|---:|---:|---
Timeout / elevated latency alerts | 46 | 32% | Often symptom-based; needs better breakdown by model/region
Streaming disconnect rate | 28 | 19% | Currently low actionability; PR 301 adds region/model splits
5xx / gateway error rate | 24 | 17% | Best signal; faster routing; often becomes incident quickly
Dedicated capacity/scheduler | 21 | 15% | Noisy around peak; needs tuned thresholds + runbook (ENG-2845)
Private control plane/auth | 12 | 8% | Lower volume but longer time-to-mitigate
Other | 13 | 9% | One-offs
Total pages | 144 | 100% | Not all pages result in customer-visible escalations

Pager-to-escalation relationship (rough)
- ~40% of pages map to a Support escalation within 60 minutes.
- ~25% of Support escalations cause a page (intended; we do not want “page every escalation”).

Observed issues
- “Escalation requested” often happens in Support channel without “promoting” to #incidents even when impact is broad.
- Some page storms are triggered by identical symptom across multiple models/regions but are not grouped (missing aggregation/roll-up).

Proposed improvements
- Add roll-up alerts by (region, model family, customer tier) and surface to Support via dashboard links rather than paging on each micro-symptom.
- Add runbook quicklinks in alert payloads (PR 301 in flight).


4) SLA vs internal SLO gaps (what customers expect vs what we can reliably hit)
Customer SLA language is being finalized in PM-612 / playbook v2; below uses the current working assumptions discussed in Support×SRE sync.

Assumed customer comms expectations (working draft)
Tier | First response (Support) | Eng/SRE engage target (when escalated) | Update cadence during active issue
---|---|---|---
Self-serve | < 4 business hours | best-effort | daily or when meaningful
Dedicated | < 1 hour (BH) | < 30 min (BH) | every 2–4 hours (active)
Private/Enterprise | < 30 min (24/7 for Sev0/P0) | < 15 min (24/7 for Sev0/P0) | hourly for Sev0/P0; every 4 hours otherwise

Internal reality (Feb 1–21)
- Business hours: generally close for Dedicated; inconsistent for Private.
- After-hours: we miss the “<15 min engage” expectation regularly when the event is not declared an incident.

Gap table (derived)
Gap | Evidence | Root cause hypothesis | Proposed fix
---|---|---|---
AH MTTA too high for enterprise P0 | Median AH MTTA 41m; multiple > 60m | escalation not incident; unclear thresholds; routing friction | tighten “declare incident” triggers; incident-bot prompt to escalate; update playbook
Update cadence inconsistent | Support asks for hourly updates; Eng provides sporadic notes | no single owner; comms thread not standardized | use #incidents for Sev0/P0; comms templates; designate incident scribe / comms buddy
TTM slow for Private SSO | Private median TTM 5h+ | dependency on customer IdP changes; unclear ownership between Security vs Private Deployments | add decision tree + required diagnostics; pre-canned “customer action” checklist; define oncall secondary for Security


5) Top escalation drivers (Support view) and impact
Table E — Top drivers (Feb 1–21)

Driver | N | Typical symptoms | Median MTTR | Notes / examples
---|---:|---|---:|---
Streaming disconnects | 16 | client sees stream cut mid-response; retry works sometimes | 7h 50m | SUP-4921; PR 18742 + PR 301 + KB page in PR 642
429 throttling / quota confusion | 14 | sudden 429s post-launch; “we didn’t change anything” | 3h 10m | SUP-4922; SDK retry/backoff PR 519; KB page in PR 642
Dedicated latency spikes | 11 | p95 latency spikes during peak; intermittent timeouts | 15h 25m | SUP-4924; noisy-neighbor suspicion; runbook refresh ENG-2845
Regional 5xx / model version issues | 9 | elevated 5xx in region; often pinned model version | 9h 05m | SUP-4925; mitigation via region failover, rollback/pin guidance
Private SSO/SAML failures | 8 | login failures after IdP change; SAML assertions | 1d 14h | SUP-4923; sensitive handling; Security + Private Deployments coordination
Other | 16 | mixed | 10h+ | includes networking edge cases


6) Where time is lost (diagnosis friction map)
We manually reviewed 12 escalations end-to-end (mixture of Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

Common friction points (ranked)
1) Missing request IDs / trace IDs
   - Adds 30–120 minutes of back-and-forth.
   - Especially painful for intermittent streaming/timeouts.
2) Missing “what changed?” context (deploy, SDK version bump, customer config change)
3) Customer environment ambiguity (Hosted vs Dedicated; region; pinned model version)
4) Lack of a single canonical runbook link for Support to follow (multiple partial docs)
5) No consistent “escalation handoff packet” in Slack/Jira (each person writes it differently)

What “good” looks like (example fields)
- Impact summary (who/what/how many requests)
- Env (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region(s), org/project
- Model name + version/pin (if applicable)
- Time window with timezone
- 3–10 representative request_id(s) or trace IDs
- Error distribution (429 vs timeout vs 5xx), sample payload sizes, streaming on/off
- Customer mitigations attempted (client retries, timeouts, region failover)


7) Proposed changes (owned actions for the sprint)
Action | Owner | Status | Expected effect
---|---|---|---
Add “escalation required fields” checklist + lint to workflow (Jira + incident-bot) | Dev Patel / Owen Phillips / Miles Thornton | In progress (ENG-2842, ENG-2843) | Reduce incomplete escalations; lower MTTA/TTM
Streaming disconnect observability (metric + dashboard + alert payload runbook links) | Allison Grant / Tomáš Novák | In progress (ENG-2844, PR 301) | Increase alert actionability; faster routing
Dedicated latency spike runbook refresh + alert tuning | Rafael Mendes / Tomáš Novák | Planned (ENG-2845) | Reduce false pages; faster mitigation
SLO toolkit views for escalation ack + mitigation | Chris Osei / Sean Gallagher | In progress (PR 88) | Weekly reporting; trend tracking; keep everyone honest
Known-issues KB pages (safe-to-share + internal diagnostics) | Priya Shah / Elliot Price | In review (PR 642) | Ticket deflection; faster customer self-mitigation
SDK default retry/backoff improvements | Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan | In review (PR 519) | Reduce 429/timeouts escalations; consistent guidance


8) Weekly reporting proposal (what we’ll track during rollout)
Metrics to review weekly (Support + SRE; 30 min)
- Escalations: count by surface (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) + tier
- MTTA: median + p90 (BH vs AH)
- TTM: median + p90
- % escalations with Complete packet
- Pages: total + % actionable (manual label for now)
- Top 3 drivers + deflection rate from KB (if measurable)

Cadence / owners
- Chris Osei to compile weekly roll-up (using SLO toolkit export once landed).
- Rafael Mendes to provide paging summary + any threshold changes.
- Dev Patel / Owen Phillips to provide escalation packet completeness + qualitative friction notes.


9) Open questions / decisions needed
- Decision: What is the explicit threshold for “declare incident” vs “support escalation” for:
  - sustained regional 5xx
  - streaming disconnect spikes
  - Dedicated latency spikes affecting multiple tenants
  - Private SSO outages
- Decision: After-hours expectations by tier (esp. Dedicated vs Private/Enterprise) and whether non-incident escalations can meet promised comms cadence.
- Process: Do we require a Jira key before paging SRE (for P1/P2), or do we allow Slack-first for P0 only?


Appendix: Notes from representative tickets
- SUP-4921 (Dedicated/Enterprise): streaming disconnects; improved by client reconnect guidance + runtime keepalive changes; major delay was missing request_id initially.
- SUP-4922 (Self-serve): 429 confusion; resolved quickly once quota dashboard reviewed; low MTTR but high ticket volume risk.
- SUP-4923 (Private): SSO change caused login failures; long MTTR driven by customer-side IdP config + Security ownership handoff.
- SUP-4924 (Dedicated): peak latency; needs better noisy-neighbor/capacity runbook; currently too much guesswork.
- SUP-4925 (Hosted/Enterprise): regional 5xx; fastest path was region failover guidance + internal incident linkage.

Notes to self (Sean)
- Once PR 88 lands, replace manual sampling with SLO export for MTTA/TTM.
- Align severity labels with playbook v2 (currently we’re using “P0/P1-like” language to avoid premature mapping).
